input_signals.name: wc_share_of_balance_sheet_growth
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), ABS(DELTA(ppent, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Holding the amount of balance-sheet expansion fixed, the share of that expansion occurring in non-cash working capital rather than in net plant predicts lower returns, because working-capital accruals are the least reliable and fastest-reversing component of growth.
input_signals.reasoning: This is deliberately a composition share bounded in [-1, 1], not a difference of two anomaly levels: it does not require ΔPPE to predict returns positively, only that it reverses less strongly than ΔWC, which is exactly the reliability ordering documented in the balance-sheet accrual decomposition. Because magnitudes are normalized away, the signal is orthogonal to the overall size of growth and isolates the accounting-versus-productive mix that the mandate targets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), add( abs( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), abs( delta( ppent, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: chronic_accrual_investment_ramp
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(capx, 1), 1)), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(ib, oancf), 0), 3))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms ramping up capital spending while having reported positive accruals in every one of the last three years are serially overinvesting behind chronically soft earnings, and this persistence — not the one-year level of free cash flow — is what predicts subsequent underperformance.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the free-cash-flow difference with a persistence interaction: the accruals theme enters as a count of consecutive accrual-positive years (0 to 3), a chronicity measure with no analogue in standard FCF, and it gates a non-negative rank of capex acceleration. Both channels retain their established negative sign, so nothing is bet against the literature, while the compounding of repeated non-cash earnings with an investment ramp identifies the firms whose growth is least likely to be validated by future cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( winsor( growth( capx, 1 ), 1 ) ), ts_sum( indicator( sub( ib, oancf ), 0 ), 3 ) )

input_signals.name: soft_asset_growth_share
input_signals.expression: RATIO(ADD(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), DELTA(COALESCE(intan, 0), 1)), ADD(ABS(ADD(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), DELTA(COALESCE(intan, 0), 1))), ABS(DELTA(ppent, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: "Accounting growth" is broader than working capital: growth in acquired intangibles is also non-verified, non-productive balance-sheet expansion, so pooling soft-asset growth against plant growth should sharpen the same composition mechanism.
input_signals.reasoning: Purchased intangibles and goodwill enter assets at negotiated values with no cash-productivity test and are the most write-down-prone assets on the balance sheet, so they belong on the accrual side of the composition rather than being ignored. Unreported intangibles are economically zero, justifying the COALESCE, and this tests whether the gen-0 winner was specifically about working capital or about soft assets generally.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( add( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), delta( coalesce( intan, 0 ), 1 ) ), add( abs( add( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), delta( coalesce( intan, 0 ), 1 ) ) ), abs( delta( ppent, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: soft_depreciation_hard_capex
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(dp, ppegt), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms investing aggressively in gross capital while depreciating that capital slowly are simultaneously expanding real assets and using the most durable income-increasing accrual choice, and this combination reverses more than either practice alone.
input_signals.reasoning: Depreciation is the single largest non-current accrual and its rate relative to the gross capital base is a direct measure of accounting aggressiveness, a channel untouched by the archive's working-capital and total-accrual constructions. Both legs are non-negative [0,1] ranks scaled by the same capital stock, so the product is monotone in each with no sign inversion, and it identifies capitalization-aggressive expanders whose reported earnings overstate the return on new capacity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( winsor( ratio( capx, ppegt ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( dp, ppegt ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: externally_financed_accrual_growth
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, DELTA(dltt, 1)), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accrual-heavy expansion that must be paid for with fresh equity and debt issuance is the least cash-validated form of growth, because neither the earnings signal nor the funding comes from operations.
input_signals.reasoning: This adds the financing dimension the archive lacks: the same accrual intensity has very different implications when internally funded versus when the firm is simultaneously tapping external capital markets, whose suppliers of funds are the least able to detect accrual inflation. Both legs are established negative predictors entered as non-negative ranks, so the claim is superadditivity in the joint corner rather than any sign reversal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( winsor( ratio( add( sstk, delta( dltt, 1 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: chronic_accounting_asset_drift
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), ADD(ABS(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), ppegt)), 3), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose operating asset base drifts over several years toward non-cash working capital and away from installed capacity are chronically substituting accounting growth for productive investment, and this slow deterioration predicts persistent underperformance.
input_signals.reasoning: The fragile unbounded working-capital-per-capacity ratio is replaced by a bounded composition level in roughly [-1, 1] whose denominator can never approach zero while the numerator is large, so asset-light firms no longer explode and the measure is directly comparable cross-sectionally. Taking a three-rather-than-five-year change of that bounded state retains the chronic-drift concept while requiring far less history, keeping coverage near the archive's 0.11, and the outer winsorization caps any residual tail influence on the Fama-MacBeth slope.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( delta( ratio( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), add( abs( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ) ), ppegt ) ), 3 ), 1 )

input_signals.name: depreciation_slowdown_with_capex_ramp
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(dp, ppegt), 1), 1))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm that slows its own depreciation rate relative to its own recent history while ramping capital spending is making an income-increasing accounting choice to flatter the returns on new capacity, and this discretionary combination predicts reversal.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-1 winner used the depreciation-rate *level*, which the critic correctly noted is dominated by industry asset-life technology rather than discretion; taking the within-firm one-year change purges the technology component and isolates the managerial choice. If this version matches or beats the level version's fmb −3.02 and alpha −0.024, the channel is genuinely about accounting discretion; if it collapses, the earlier result was capital-intensity technology and the family should be redirected.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( winsor( delta( ratio( dp, ppegt ), 1 ), 1 ) ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( capx, ppegt ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: soft_assets_per_worker_share
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(act, che), emp), 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(act, che), emp), 1)), ABS(DELTA(RATIO(ppent, emp), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Scaling by real input rather than by assets, growth concentrated in non-cash current assets per worker rather than in plant per worker identifies firms whose books are expanding faster than their productive organization, and this composition predicts low returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the archived hiring interaction entirely: labor now enters as the deflator that makes both the accounting leg and the productive leg per-unit-of-real-input intensities, so the signal is about capital and receivable/inventory deepening per worker rather than about hiring growth as a moderator. It therefore has no directional conflict with the gen-1 employment result and tests a genuinely new normalization — whether the composition mechanism is sharper when measured against real operating scale instead of the balance-sheet total that the accrual leg itself inflates.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( ratio( sub( act, che ), emp ), 1 ), add( abs( delta( ratio( sub( act, che ), emp ), 1 ) ), abs( delta( ratio( ppent, emp ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: cashflow_payback_on_capex_program
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(oancf, 3), ADD(ABS(DELTA(oancf, 3)), TS_SUM(capx, 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A three-year capital program that fails to raise the firm's own operating cash flow has produced accounting assets rather than productive capacity, and the marginal cash payback on invested dollars predicts returns positively.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the cash-flow *level* with its three-year *change* removes the profitability component that FF5's RMW absorbs: the numerator is now the incremental cash generated over exactly the window in which the capital was deployed, making this a firm-specific marginal-return-on-investment measure rather than a profitability-minus-investment composite. Firms with identical cash-flow profitability and identical capex intensity are separated by whether the investment actually moved cash flow, which is the interaction the theme calls for.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( oancf, 3 ), add( abs( delta( oancf, 3 ) ), ts_sum( capx, 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: soft_growth_vs_capex_flow
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), capx))
input_signals.hypothesis: The productive leg of the growth composition is better measured by the gross capital spending flow than by the change in net plant, because net plant is itself contaminated by the depreciation accrual and by disposals.
input_signals.reasoning: Every composition signal in the archive uses ΔPPE, which equals capex minus depreciation minus disposals, so its "productive" leg mixes real investment with exactly the accounting-discretion channel the depreciation signals showed to be independently priced. Replacing it with capex isolates verified cash outlay on capacity, and capex-based signals have shown the archive's best coverage (0.127), so this should improve both the purity of the mechanism and the sample.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), add( abs( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), capx ) )

input_signals.name: wc_buildup_without_prior_capacity
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), TS_SUM(LAG(capx, 1), 2)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Working capital expansion is economically legitimate when it follows a capacity build-out and illegitimate when it appears without one, so the relevant investment context is the firm's capital spending in the *preceding* years, not the current year.
input_signals.reasoning: Real expansion has a natural sequence — capacity is installed first, then receivables and inventory scale with the resulting output — so contemporaneous matching, used by every archive composition signal, mismeasures which working-capital builds are supported. Pairing the current accrual build against the prior two years of capex tests that lead-lag structure directly, and read alongside Signal 5 it identifies whether the timing of the real-investment context matters at all.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), add( abs( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), ts_sum( lag( capx, 1 ), 2 ) ) )

input_signals.name: net_deployment_payback
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(oancf, 3), ADD(ABS(DELTA(oancf, 3)), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 3)))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash generated should be measured against the net resources a firm actually tied up — cash capital expenditure plus working capital absorbed, minus working capital released — so that accrual-shaped deployment is charged as a cost and accrual releases are credited.
input_signals.reasoning: Removing the ABS around the working-capital term fixes the internal inconsistency the critic identified: a firm with rising cash flow that simultaneously liquidates receivables and inventory now shows a *smaller* deployment base and ranks in the long leg, exactly as the economics require, while an accrual-absorbing grower is penalized. Cumulative capex keeps the denominator positive in the overwhelming majority of firm-years, and the outer winsorization caps the rare cases where a very large working-capital release dominates the capital program.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( delta( oancf, 3 ), add( abs( delta( oancf, 3 ) ), add( ts_sum( capx, 3 ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 3 ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: noncurrent_soft_growth_share
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(at, act), ppent), 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(SUB(SUB(at, act), ppent), 1)), ABS(DELTA(ppent, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Growth concentrated in non-current operating assets other than plant — capitalized costs, other long-term assets, purchased intangibles — is the least verifiable form of expansion and reverses more sharply than growth in physical capacity.
input_signals.reasoning: This changes the accrual bucket rather than the window: instead of working capital, the numerator isolates the long-lived residual asset category that carries the lowest measurement reliability because it accumulates costs management chose to capitalize rather than expense, and which no archive signal has targeted. It uses only balance-sheet inputs, so it should retain the 0.11-plus coverage of the composition family while testing whether the mechanism lives in current or non-current soft assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( sub( sub( at, act ), ppent ), 1 ), add( abs( delta( sub( sub( at, act ), ppent ), 1 ) ), abs( delta( ppent, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: capitalization_outpacing_expensing
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), 1)), dp))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose intangible and goodwill balances grow rapidly relative to the total depreciation and amortization they recognize are accumulating unexpensed soft assets, and the eventual impairment of those balances predicts negative returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the mechanical blend with a new hypothesis about the balance between capitalization and expense recognition — the accrual choice with the longest fuse — measured against the soft asset stock that investment activity creates. Unlike the archive's depreciation-rate signals, which scale expense by physical plant, this scales soft-asset accumulation by total expense recognition, so it flags firms building a stock of assets against which almost nothing is being charged to income.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( add( coalesce( intan, 0 ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), 1 ), add( abs( delta( add( coalesce( intan, 0 ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), 1 ) ), dp ) )

input_signals.name: unexpected_wc_build_vs_capex
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), 3)), ADD(ABS(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), 3))), capx))
input_signals.hypothesis: Only *unexpected* working-capital expansion is mispriced; a firm whose operating model routinely absorbs working capital as it grows has a build the market already anticipates, whereas a build well above the firm's own recent norm signals deteriorating growth quality.
input_signals.reasoning: Every composition signal in the archive uses the raw accrual level, which conflates the firm's structural working-capital intensity with a genuine surprise, and structural intensity is a stable characteristic that a rational market prices. Benchmarking the current build against the firm's own three-year average build isolates the surprise component while keeping capex as the cash-verified denominator, which is a substantive economic refinement rather than a window change.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), ma( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), 3 ) ), add( abs( sub( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), ma( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), 3 ) ) ), capx ) )

input_signals.name: synthetic_cashflow_payback
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 3), ADD(ABS(DELTA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 3)), TS_SUM(capx, 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The cash payback on a capital program is the archive's strongest mechanism, and it should survive when operating cash flow is reconstructed from earnings, depreciation and the working-capital accrual instead of read off the cash-flow statement.
input_signals.reasoning: Reported `oancf` is the binding coverage constraint in the payback family (0.056–0.065 versus 0.11 for balance-sheet signals) because it requires four consecutive statement-of-cash-flows observations; the Sloan-style reconstruction ib + dp − ΔWC uses items available far more broadly and for a much longer history. This is simultaneously a coverage repair and a genuine robustness test: if the payback result holds with the synthetic measure, the mechanism is about cash conversion rather than about the post-1988 subsample in which cash-flow statements exist.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), 3 ), add( abs( delta( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), 3 ) ), ts_sum( capx, 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: other_operating_asset_build_vs_capex
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(SUB(at, act), ppent), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(SUB(SUB(SUB(at, act), ppent), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1)), capx))
input_signals.hypothesis: Growth concentrated in other long-term operating assets — capitalized costs, deferred charges, and miscellaneous assets outside plant, current assets, and purchased intangibles — is the least verifiable form of expansion and predicts low returns relative to growth in cash capital spending.
input_signals.reasoning: Moving from the cash-flow statement's net `aoloch` residual to an explicitly asset-side balance-sheet bucket removes the sign ambiguity the critic identified: a high value can now only mean other operating assets grew, never that liabilities shrank. Excluding purchased intangibles also removes the acquirer-driven zero-mass contamination that left `noncurrent_soft_growth_share` and `capitalization_outpacing_expensing` cross-sectionally significant but portfolio-dead, and the capex denominator is the specification that has produced the family's best joint evidence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( sub( sub( sub( at, act ), ppent ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), 1 ), add( abs( delta( sub( sub( sub( at, act ), ppent ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), 1 ) ), capx ) )

input_signals.name: full_accrual_adjusted_payback
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), DELTA(SUB(SUB(SUB(at, act), ppent), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1)), 3), ADD(ABS(DELTA(SUB(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), DELTA(SUB(SUB(SUB(at, act), ppent), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1)), 3)), TS_SUM(capx, 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The payback on a capital program should be measured after removing *all* accrual categories from earnings, including the non-current operating assets in which capitalized costs accumulate, not just working capital.
input_signals.reasoning: The synthetic reconstruction that won gen 4 subtracts only ΔWC, leaving capitalized-cost accruals inside the numerator; the other-operating-asset bucket was independently the strongest cross-sectional channel in the archive (fmb −3.80) even though it carried no standalone spread, which is exactly the profile of a variable that belongs as a correction term rather than as a signal. Purging it should make the numerator a cleaner measure of cash actually generated per dollar of capacity installed and sharpen both the slope and the spread.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( sub( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), delta( sub( sub( sub( at, act ), ppent ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), 1 ) ), 3 ), add( abs( delta( sub( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), delta( sub( sub( sub( at, act ), ppent ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), 1 ) ), 3 ) ), ts_sum( capx, 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: acquisition_inclusive_payback
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 3), ADD(ABS(DELTA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 3)), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), TS_SUM(COALESCE(aqc, 0), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that grow by buying assets rather than building them must be charged for that deployment too; measuring cash improvement against capex alone flatters serial acquirers, who are precisely the firms whose growth is accounting rather than productive.
input_signals.reasoning: The winning payback denominator counts only internally built capacity, so an acquirer that spends nothing on capex and generates no incremental cash can look identical to a genuinely capital-light compounder. Adding cumulative acquisition outlays makes the denominator the firm's total real deployment and directly tests whether the inorganic channel — weak as a standalone signal (`inorganic_growth_accrual_stack`, fmb −0.81) — matters once embedded in the payback structure, with zero being the economically correct value for non-acquirers.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), 3 ), add( abs( delta( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), 3 ) ), add( ts_sum( capx, 3 ), ts_sum( coalesce( aqc, 0 ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: nonoverlapping_persistent_payback
input_signals.expression: RATIO(MIN(DELTA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 1), LAG(DELTA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 2), 1)), ADD(ABS(MIN(DELTA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 1), LAG(DELTA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 2), 1))), TS_SUM(capx, 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A capital program is validated only if accrual-adjusted cash flow improved in the early years of the program *and* again most recently; requiring the improvement in two non-overlapping sub-periods separates durable productivity gains from a single favorable year.
input_signals.reasoning: The two legs are now disjoint — the most recent one-year change and the change over the two years that preceded it — so their correlation is far from unity and the conjunction is informative rather than a horizon reparameterization of the same difference. Economically this is the long-side analogue of the persistence device that produced the archive's best short-side spread: the firm must show cash improvement at two separate points in the life of the same capital program, which no single endpoint-to-endpoint difference can verify.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( min( delta( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), 1 ), lag( delta( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), 2 ), 1 ) ), add( abs( min( delta( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), 1 ), lag( delta( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), 2 ), 1 ) ) ), ts_sum( capx, 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: per_worker_payback_on_capex
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), emp), 3), ADD(ABS(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), emp), 3)), TS_SUM(RATIO(capx, emp), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-flow gains that merely reflect a bigger organization are not evidence of productive capital; only an improvement in accrual-adjusted cash flow *per worker* per dollar invested per worker shows that the capital program raised productivity rather than just scale.
input_signals.reasoning: The tax channel is abandoned because the critic is correct that `txp` is an accrual balance rather than cash taxes paid, so it cannot serve as an independent verification channel; headcount is the real-input measure that management cannot book without paying wages, making it the available substitute. Deflating both the cash improvement and the capital outlay by employment converts the payback measure from a scale statement into a productivity statement, which is a different economic quantity and directly addresses whether growth is real.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( ratio( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), emp ), 3 ), add( abs( delta( ratio( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ) ), emp ), 3 ) ), ts_sum( ratio( capx, emp ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: full_accrual_payback_total_deployment
input_signals.expression: RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), DELTA(SUB(SUB(SUB(at, act), ppent), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1)), 3), ADD(ABS(DELTA(SUB(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), DELTA(SUB(SUB(SUB(at, act), ppent), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1)), 3)), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), TS_SUM(COALESCE(aqc, 0), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The cleanest statement of the theme is cash generated — after purging every accrual category from earnings — per dollar of total real resources committed, whether those resources were spent building capacity or buying it.
input_signals.reasoning: Gen 5 tested the numerator correction (full accrual purge, fmb +4.32) and the denominator correction (charging acquirers for inorganic deployment, talpha +4.92) separately, and each improved a different metric relative to the gen-4 winner; the two operate on opposite sides of the ratio and address non-overlapping measurement gaps, so combining them is the natural consolidation rather than a third variant. Both corrections carry zero as the economically correct value for firms without other-asset builds or acquisitions, so the change binds exactly where the mismeasurement was.
